snippet.title: Does Duolingo Work? Here's the Science Behind It
snippet.description:
Does Duolingo work? Is Duolingo actually effective for learning a language?

Yes, Duolingo does work. And the answer comes down to learning science.

Duolingo is built on decades of research in psychology, cognitive science, and neuroscience. Instead of asking learners to memorize vocabulary lists or grammar rules, the app uses evidence-based learning techniques that help people remember information longer and use it in real conversations.

Our courses are developed by a team of learning designers, curriculum experts, and learning scientists, including researchers with PhDs in fields like cognitive science, psychology, linguistics, and education.

In this video, Parker (Learning Designer) and Audrey (Learning Scientist) explain the five core learning science principles behind Duolingo:
• Retrieval practice
 • Noticing patterns
 • Spaced repetition
 • The zone of proximal development
 • Communicative competence

You'll also see how features like Practice Hub, Explain My Answer, DuoRadio, Speaking Adventures, and Video Call put these principles into practice.

Whether you're wondering "Does Duolingo work?", "Is Duolingo effective?", "How does Duolingo teach languages?", or "Can Duolingo help you become fluent?", this video explains the science behind the app.

snippet.title: Duolingo and LinkedIn Join Forces
snippet.description:
George leads Business Development at Duolingo, where he built the function from the ground up. Since joining in 2020, he’s helped forge many of Duolingo’s most impactful partnerships—spanning brand partnerships, monetization deals, and product integrations—and has spun up new business lines such as Ad Sales and IP Licensing. Before Duolingo, George spent six years at Google Play, where he led Business Development for subscription and Media & Entertainment apps. He started his career as a strategy consultant at Boston Consulting Group, grew up in Lebanon, and lives in NYC. George holds a Bachelor of Computer Engineering from the American University in Beirut and an MBA from Harvard Business School.

snippet.title: Building Duolingo: One Test at a Time
snippet.description:
Natalia Castillejo is a Director of Product Management at Duolingo. Since joining in 2016, she has played a key role in building and evolving Duolingo’s language learning and monetization products. Originally from Venezuela, she is passionate about making sure Duolingo is perfect for everyont thanks to rigours A/B testing. This method of approach enables our learning scientists to surface and tess different features to learn which one performs better; always using real user data. This helps teams make informed decisions, reduce guesswork, and continuously improve the user experience within our learning app.
